ending_first.ending: Hetta presents the false village weight at midwinter without a public challenge, tells only Bram that she has read the metal, leaves the piece unbroken so the levy continues, and that night measures the shortfall against a true work-bar.
ending_first.cost: Bram keeps paying in breath, warmth, and his right hand; Hetta becomes the second keeper of the lie by choice; the lane keeps its year in ignorance; the household continues without being restored.
ending_first.final_image: Hetta's hands on the forge balance as the village weight tips short against a true bar; a scrap naming the difference goes into the niche; Bram stands in the doorway and does not cross; the fire is banked; neither speaks.

jacket_copy: Three weeks before midwinter the village weight is gone from its niche above the slack-tub. Highkettle has paid iron for three generations to keep the pass open and the winter grain coming; without the relic at the rite, the Hold closes both. Olla puts the fetch on the forge-house. Bram, who raised Hetta at the anvil, says she can walk it. She is twenty-four, already a smith in the work, and she treats an empty niche as a job with a date. The high pass will cost her in cold and hunger. The raiders on the poorer slopes are hungry people, not an army. She is good at retrieval and at reading metal. She is bad at deciding what she owes the man who taught her. What she brings home will have a weight, and no one is coming to lift it for her.

s01.text: Forty years back, after the original presentation-weight cracked in a famine winter, Bram forged a replacement and bound into it a levy on his breath, warmth, and right hand so the Hold compact would hold.

s02.text: The work fed children that winter, and he never found a year when telling seemed cheaper than silence.

s03.text: He raised Hetta from ten at the forge, teaching her until at twenty-four she is a smith in all but name.

s04.text: Highkettle has paid iron for three generations: present the village weight and tithe at midwinter, or forfeit the pass and winter grain-right.

s05.text: The Hold inspects authenticity only if the object is challenged or broken, and a non-original holds only while the bound smith pays.

s06.text: Three weeks before this midwinter, hungry raiders from poorer slopes take the weight from its niche above the slack-tub.

s07.text: Olla names the theft and the days left, and puts the fetch on the forge-house because that is where the iron lives.

s08.text: Hetta treats the empty niche as a job with a walking-time and accepts Bram's sending without asking why he will not go.

s09.text: She must bring the weight home before the rite, or the hamlet loses a year of pass and grain it cannot replace.

s10.text: He sends her untold because the levy keeps him off the pass, and because other hands might break the piece or read it.

s11.text: The village can spare no mounts or second walker, and the winter pass will exact a bodily cost she carries alone.

s12.text: She walks the pass, pays in cold and hunger, and takes the piece from people who need metal or a bargain for grain.

s13.text: On the return the piece sits wrong against her spine, short of the mass her hand expects.

s14.text: Checking it for travel-damage, she reads quench-line, bloom, and a stamp forty years too young, and knows the weight is his early forgery before anyone confesses.

s15.text: She comes home already knowing, so recovery has spent the chance to hear him first, and his reasons can only arrive as defence.

s16.text: Faced with her questions on quench, bloom, and stamp-date, Bram tells of the cracked original, the famine, three nights, a failed harvest, the binding, and the child she was when telling became another use.

s17.text: The old reasons stay audible as a kindness that fed a winter, and they do not defend forty years of silence or his using her walk.

s18.text: Before the rite she must choose: present a known-false weight, break it and starve the lane, or tell the steward and still not free him unless the iron breaks too.

s19.text: She presents the piece at the midwinter ground, tells only Bram she has read it, and does not break it; the steward takes it unchallenged while Bram stands behind her paying.

s20.text: The lane keeps its year, the levy continues, and she becomes by choice the second keeper of a lie the village will not hear.

s21.text: That night she sets the village weight against a true work-bar, writes the shortfall, and puts the scrap in the niche beside the piece.

s22.text: Bram watches from the doorway and does not cross; she banks the fire; they do not speak; the household continues unrestored.

s23.text: He pays in body, she in complicity, the lane in ignorance; no one is rescued, and no one is told whether she was right.
